predecessors.name: Roman Empire
predecessors.text: 'most of the East (Egypt, Syria and Asia)': Egypt, Syria, Lebanon, Israel and Anatolia as the Roman Empire held them in 259

successors.name: Palmyrene Empire
successors.text: Syria, Phoenice and the Levant: Odaenathus 'sided with the Emperor and marched on Emesa'; his authority later 'extended from the Pontic coast in the north to Palestine in the south' (Odaenathus page)

ledger.x: August 260: Macrianus's sons are declared emperors in the East.
early 261: Macrianus and Macrianus Minor leave for Europe and Quietus stays at Emesa with Balista.

wars.name: Usurpation of Macrianus and Quietus
wars.outcome: Macrianus and Macrianus Minor marched to Europe in early 261 and were defeated and killed in the Balkans in spring 261; Quietus and Balista, left at Emesa, were taken by Odaenathus's approach: the Emesans killed Quietus and Balista was executed in autumn 261.

certainty.note: The pages name regions only (Egypt, Syria, Asia); no frontier.
